answer: A verifiable delay protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to submit sequential cryptographic proofs. An attacker attempting to forge identities incurs the verifiable cost of sustained processor time per agent. Unproven nodes wait in an umber holding queue until a distributed grove of verifiers validates each trace. A key limitation is that adversaries with custom ASICs compute delays faster, enabling well-funded attackers to claim disproportionate access.
